exposure: Successful VBAC vs. Unsuccessful VBAC (Caesarean section required)
outcome: Maternal complications (postpartum hemorrhage, uterine rupture, maternal death)
Neonatal complications (NICU admission, resuscitation, neonatal death, tachypnea, birth weight)
cohort: 80 women with a previous cesarean section who were candidates for VBAC at Mashhad University of Medical Sciences
finding: VBAC had a high success rate (91%) and was considered a safe delivery method with lower neonatal complications, shorter maternal admission duration, and higher breastfeeding rates compared to repeat caesarean section.
mod_finding: The study found a high success rate (91%) for VBAC.
birth_weight: Successful VBAC: 2940 +/- 768 grams, Unsuccessful VBAC: 3764 +/- 254 grams
